newsitem.title: UK: Widespread powers proposed for Scottish Parliament.
newsitem.headline: Widespread powers proposed for Scottish Parliament.

text.p: The British Labour government's policy White Paper on Scottish devolution, published on Wednesday, gives full details of what powers it envisages being given to an Edinburgh Parliament which would start sitting in 2000.
The following is a summary of the details --
POWERS TO BE DEVOLVED TO EDINBURGH
Responsibility for
- The National Health Service in Scotland and public and mental health.
- Education from the under fives to universities, and training.
- Local government structure and finance, social work, building control and the planning framework.
- Economic development, financial assistance for business, trade and export promotion, inward investment, tourism, administration of EU structural funds and a range of transport matters.
- The criminal justice system including police and prisons, fire services, legal aid and civil defence.
- Environmental protection, water, sewerage, flood prevention and coastal protection.
- Sport and the arts.
- Law-making powers over a wide range of matters which affect Scotland. POWERS TO REMAIN WITH THE UK PARLIAMENT
-- Constitutional issues, including electoral law, the civil service and the award of honours.
-- Foreign policy, including the ability to conclude EU and other international agreements in areas devolved to Scotland.
-- Defence and national security.
-- Border controls, including immigration and nationality.
-- Fiscal, economic and monetary policy.

-- Common markets for UK goods and services, including laws on companies, insurance, corporate insolvency and intellectual property, regulation of financial institutions and financial services, competition policy, consumer protection and the regulation of energy supply industries.
-- Employment legislation, including industrial relations, equal opportunities and health and safety.
-- Social security policy and administration, including pensions.
-- Regulation of certain professions, including the medical, dental, nursing and other health professions, vets, architects, auditors, estate agents and insolvency practitioners.
-- Transport safety and regulation.

-- Miscellaneous, including UK research councils, nuclear safety, control of medicines, broadcasting regulations and film classification, gambling, abortion, human fertilisation and embryology, genetics, xenotransplantation (transplanting animal organs into humans) and equality legislation. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 7767
